story.title: Israelis Vote in Crucial Election Amid Security Concerns and Political Rivalries
story.summary: Israelis are set to vote in a pivotal election that follows the October 7 attacks by Hamas. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership and national security are central themes in this closely contested race against former Israeli Army Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot. Polls indicate a tight competition, with Netanyahu emphasizing his security credentials while facing accusations of politicizing the Iran threat.

timeline_highlights.title: Israel Displaces 250 Palestinian Families in Hebron Following Soldier Deaths
timeline_highlights.summary: In response to the killing of two Israeli soldiers by Palestinian gunmen at a checkpoint, Israel has initiated a significant operation in Hebron, displacing around 250 Palestinian families. This action is part of a broader clampdown in the West Bank, coinciding with upcoming elections in Israel. The United Nations has raised concerns about potential 'ethnic cleansing' and described the operation as collective punishment, which it deems a violation of international law.
key_facts: Two Israeli soldiers were killed by Palestinian gunmen at a checkpoint in Hebron.
Israel has displaced around 250 Palestinian families as part of a military operation.
The operation has raised concerns of 'ethnic cleansing' from the United Nations.
The actions coincide with Israeli elections scheduled for October 26, 2026.

explore_lenses.label: What are Israelis actually voting for?
explore_lenses.title: A party vote that determines coalition leverage
explore_lenses.summary: Israelis vote for party lists, not directly for a prime minister. The decisive question is which parties clear the entry threshold and whether a bloc can assemble a majority in the 120-seat Knesset.

claims.text: The election for the 26th Knesset is scheduled for Tuesday, October 27, 2026; official final results are due by November 4.
A party must receive at least 3.25% of the vote to enter the Knesset, and a governing coalition requires support from at least 61 of its 120 members.
This makes smaller lists consequential: a party narrowly crossing or missing the threshold can change coalition arithmetic even if Likud or Eisenkot’s Yashar! finishes first.

explore_lenses.label: What do Netanyahu and Eisenkot argue?
explore_lenses.title: Security credentials versus accountability and service
explore_lenses.summary: Both leading camps put security at the center, but they offer competing accounts of leadership after October 7 and differ on domestic priorities such as ultra-Orthodox military exemptions.

claims.text: Netanyahu’s supporters cite his security and economic record and his relationships with foreign leaders; opponents argue that policy and security failures before the October 7, 2023 attack, and his handling of subsequent wars, warrant replacing him.

Eisenkot, a former military chief and former observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet, resigned from that body after accusing Netanyahu of lacking a clear strategy; he presents himself as a moderate alternative but remains hawkish on security.

Eisenkot’s Yashar! supports equal military service and a state commission of inquiry into the October 7 attack, while Netanyahu’s coalitions have depended on ultra-Orthodox parties seeking continued exemptions for religious students.

explore_lenses.label: What happens if no bloc wins 61 seats?
explore_lenses.title: Coalition talks, caretaker rule, or another election
explore_lenses.summary: After official results, Israel’s president consults parliamentary factions and assigns a Knesset member the task of forming a government. A deadlock could keep the outgoing government in a caretaker role and ultimately trigger a new election.

claims.text: Within seven days of publication of official results, the president must assign the task of forming a government to a willing Knesset member after consulting the parliamentary groups.
The first designated candidate has 28 days to form a government, with presidential extensions totaling no more than 14 additional days; a proposed government must then win the Knesset’s confidence.

Forecast: the European Parliament Research Service assessed before the vote that neither major camp was assured of 61 seats and that the fragmented opposition and reluctance of mainstream Jewish opposition parties to formally partner with Arab factions increase the risk of stalemate or repeat elections.
If no government is formed, the outgoing government continues performing its functions until a new government is established; the legal process can eventually lead to elections within 90 days.

story_report.summary: Israelis are due to vote on Oct. 27 in the first national election since the Hamas attacks of Oct. 7, 2023, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s leadership and national security at the center of the contest. Polls indicate a close race between Netanyahu and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot. The ballot will determine the makeup of the 120-seat Knesset, but the next government will depend on which candidate can assemble support from a majority of its members after the results are certified.

sections.heading: Knesset Threshold Shapes Coalition Math
sections.body: The election is for the 26th Knesset, and official final results are due by Nov. 4. Parties need at least 3.25% of the vote to enter parliament, while a governing coalition needs the support of at least 61 of the Knesset’s 120 members. That means the outcome for smaller lists can alter coalition arithmetic even if Netanyahu’s Likud or Eisenkot’s Yashar! wins the most seats; the largest party is not automatically entitled to form the government.

sections.heading: Security Record Defines Netanyahu-Eisenkot Contest
sections.body: Netanyahu’s supporters point to his security and economic record and his relationships with foreign leaders. His opponents argue that failures before the Oct. 7 attack and his handling of the subsequent wars justify replacing him. Eisenkot, a former army chief and former observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet, resigned after accusing the prime minister of lacking a clear strategy; he presents himself as a moderate alternative while retaining hawkish security positions. Yashar! also backs equal military service and a state inquiry into the attack.

sections.heading: Government Formation Begins After Results
sections.body: Within seven days of publication of the official results, Israel’s president must consult parliamentary groups and assign a willing Knesset member to form a government. The first designated candidate receives 28 days, with possible presidential extensions totaling up to 14 more days, and any proposed government must then win the Knesset’s confidence. If no government is formed, the outgoing government remains in office until a replacement is established, and the process can eventually result in another election within 90 days.

unresolved.text: It remains unclear whether parties near the electoral threshold, Arab-led parties or a possible unity arrangement will provide a workable majority. Before the vote, an assessment found neither major camp assured of 61 seats and warned that fragmentation could produce stalemate or repeat elections.
Campaign pledges do not establish which security, conscription or inquiry policies either leader could carry out, because coalition partners may constrain those decisions.

The victory has sparked celebrations among supporters of the movement, although the new leaders face numerous challenges ahead.
